meta.goal: Run the Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 checkpoint on two RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB each, sm_120) with tensor-parallel tp=2 over P2P. Dependency policy (revised 2026-09-25, user decision): one allowed C runtime dependency — NVIDIA NCCL for the 2-GPU collective ops (hand-rolled 2-node design kept as the recorded fallback, CHG-0005); no-Python-stack preserved, 2.5 MB promise re-stated as binary + libnccl. Preserves the single-active-request DSpark losslessness property and the existing serving surface.

subsystems.name: Device initialization & context model
subsystems.why: The whole process today establishes exactly one 'current device' (thread-local cudaSetDevice in RuntimeImpl::initialize) and every kernel/stream/graph inherits it. The dual-GPU design decision (stream-scoped launches vs per-context setDevice; how many CUDA contexts coexist in one process) is made here.
checklist: RuntimeConfig.device_id (single int) -> device list + tp size
ModelEngine::load cudaGetDeviceCount gate (currently >=1) -> >= tp, and the requested ids must exist
Runtime property queries (SM count, mem clock, bus width, PCI bus id) per device
device_health: note_cuda_error/device_lost are process-global; decide fail-fast (recommended: process death on any GPU error, matching current ops) vs isolate
Confirm CUDA 'current device' is thread-local and document which threads may touch which device (server worker thread, HTTP threads doing submit-time memcpy, lmcache sidecar process)

subsystems.name: Paged KV cache
subsystems.why: One flat pool per of {K,V} (plus int8 scale pools, windowed ring tables, per-sequence block tables) on a single device. KV heads must be split across the two devices; everything built on top (paging, prefix sharing, admission, metrics, lmcache) reads those pools.
checklist: k_pool/v_pool layout [slots, blocks, block_size, kv_heads, head_dim] -> per-device pool holding kv_heads/2 each (or by slot, if head split is uneven)
Block tables: one per device pool; logical block numbering shared, physical independent
int8 KV scale pools (k_scale/v_scale) follow the same split
Windowed (SWA) ring slots and d_win_tables per pool
Prefix sharing refcounts are per physical pool (blocks are never shared across devices; a logical prefix = two halves)
Admission: KV capacity = min over pools (a session needs blocks in every pool it touches)
Auto-sizing budget (80% free VRAM in examples; server formula in ModelEngine) becomes a per-device budget
free_kv_blocks / prefix-cache metrics per pool

subsystems.name: Gated-DeltaNet recurrent state
subsystems.why: 48 of 64 Qwen3.8 layers are GDN and carry per-sequence recurrent state (fp32 lin_state + bf16 conv state) allocated at open_session on one device. The state is per value-head, so it splits cleanly across GPUs -- but every snapshot/restore/rollback path must follow.
checklist: lin_state / lin_conv_state allocation in open_session: split by linear_v_heads (24/24 with 48 heads) or by block convention (gdn_qh_block)
All snapshot paths: prefix-cache pinned-host snapshots (~205 MB on 27B), dflash spec save/restore snapshots, packed-decode bf16 compaction
Prefill recurrent-state initialization (conv state zeroing) per device
Verify no cross-head coupling in the GDN update (it must be independent per v-head or the split is invalid)

subsystems.name: MoE router & expert dispatch
subsystems.why: MoEEngine allocates its scratch (router logits, top-k ids, weights, counts) on the current device and all expert weights live on that device. Qwen3.8-27B is dense_ffn (n_experts=1, top_k=1) so it takes the dense special-case; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B would split 256 experts.
checklist: Scratch buffers per MoEEngine instance (one per device)
27B: single 'expert' = one big SwiGLU FFN -> column-split gate/up, row-split down (see layout appendix)
35B-A3B: expert residency split (E/2 per device) incl. expert_cache_slots budget and async_expert_prefetch per device
Router GEMM: input hidden is full on both devices -> replicate the router or run on device 0 and broadcast; counts/dispatch lists are then per device
launch_moe_expert_ffn* kernels: dispatch only this device's experts

subsystems.name: Weight loading & conversion
subsystems.why: Every loader mallocs the complete model into one device (17.9 GB > 16 GB). Loaders must place each tensor per the ownership map, including the opportunistic extra-format copies (o_fp4/down_fp4/wo_fp4/gate_fp4) that are currently gated on one device's free VRAM.
checklist: Per-tensor ownership map (P3 deliverable) consumed by all three loaders (GGUF, compressed-tensors, flat .bin)
GGUF quantized-in-VRAM experts: split by expert index; dequant scratch per device
Free-VRAM preflight gates become per-device decisions (an fp4 copy may fit on one card and not the other)
DSpark drafter placement (replicate vs split) per CHG-0030
Vision tower placement per CHG-0031
runtime/tools/convert_qwen35.py: output layout must support split placement (or prove it doesn't need to)

subsystems.name: Decode hot path (single/packed token)
subsystems.why: The token loop: embed -> 64 layers (16 attention + 48 GDN) -> final norm -> lm_head -> argmax, with 4 forked streams, events, one decode graph per session (parked per session), adaptive n_splits sized from SM count, and a recursive device_mutex that serializes capture against legacy-stream work. All of it is one-context today.
checklist: Streams stream/stream_k/stream_v/stream_pf: per-device sets; cross-device event pairs at all-reduce points
Decode graph capture (cu_graph + per-session parking lot): capture-on-two-contexts rules; P2P memcpy nodes need peer access ENABLED at capture time (R5)
Prefill graph and dflash verify graph: same treatment
adaptive n_splits / split tiers: sized for 170 SM (5090); 48 SM cards need retuned constants (kernel subsystem)
lm_head: row-split by vocab + cross-device argmax (greedy) / Gumbel-max (temperature)
device_mutex semantics with two contexts (the documented capture-poisoning hazard is per-context legacy-stream sync; restate the invariants)
Packed decode (decode_packed, graph tiers up to 32 rows): per-device row handling + all-reduce per layer group

subsystems.name: Batched/chunked prefill
subsystems.why: 5.6k-line batched prefill: fused qkvg grouped GEMM, NVFP4/FP8/Int8 GEMM families, chunked prefill, multi-prompt ingestion, DFlash context buffers. Same tensor split as decode, but GEMMs are row-split and their outputs feed the per-device state; the verify (dflash) pass spans both.
checklist: Fused qkvg operand [2*qdim + 2*kvdim, H]: split rows per q/kv head groups
Grouped/batched GEMM split-K variants: partial sums must recombine with the same numerics decision as decode (R2)
Chunked prefill windows and GDN state continuation across windows, per device
ingest_prompts_packed (multi-session): each session's state on both pools
Prefill graph tiers: per-device or hybrid capture

subsystems.name: ContinuousBatchEngine & sessions
subsystems.why: One worker thread drives the single device; admission tickets count KV blocks from one pool; prefix-cache entries hold recurrent-state snapshots in pinned HOST memory (device-agnostic); the DSpark drafter and the vision tower are extra models with their own residency; the lmcache sidecar is a FORKED process with its own CUDA setup.
checklist: Worker: one thread driving both devices (streams, not setDevice) vs one thread per device -- decide (one thread is simpler; streams make it device-independent)
Admission: capacity = min over the two KV pools; waiting tickets unchanged
open_session/close_session: per-pool block allocation + per-device GDN state
DSpark: drafter residency (CHG-0030); verify pass on both devices; the byte-lossless-vs-AR gate must be re-proven inside tp=2 (R2)
Prefix cache: snapshots become per-device pairs; LRU policy unchanged (host-resident)
Vision tower: run on one device and P2P-broadcast embeddings, or replicate (CHG-0031)
lmcache sidecar: its own device assumptions; likely defer the dual-GPU KV tier to v2 (CHG-0017)

subsystems.name: Stats, thermals, metrics
subsystems.why: query_gpu_stats switches to one device for cudaMemGetInfo (NVML side already resolves by PCI bus id -- device-ordinal independent, good). The thermal governor paces from one card's temperature; /metrics and /v1/info report one GPU.
checklist: Per-device GpuStats (both cards in /metrics: vram, temp, power, clock)
/v1/info: report tp size and per-GPU names (NVIDIA's own docs: 5060 Ti = sm_120, 16 GB, 48 SM)
Thermal governor: per-card pacing (consumer cards have low TDP; both may throttle independently) or max-temp policy -- decide
device_healthy(): with two cards, one dead context = server down (align with CHG-0034 decision)

subsystems.name: CUDA kernels (471 __global__, 273 top-level launch_*)
subsystems.why: Most kernels are device-agnostic (pointers in, current context runs them) and need NO code change under tp=2 -- they just run once per device on that device's slice. The audit target is the minority with 5090-shaped assumptions: grid sizes, n_splits tiers, occupancy targets, hardcoded SM counts, and any kernel that reads a tensor larger than one device's slice would hold.
checklist: Sweep for hardcoded 170/SM-derived constants (n_splits tiers, block counts, chunk sizes)

Kernels that address whole tensors (embed, lm_head, qkvg fused operand): confirm they take the per-device slice pointer from the split map, not a full-tensor base+offset that crosses the device boundary
flash-decode split counts (adaptive_nsplits_for): retune for 48 SM
MoE dispatch kernels: per-device expert ranges
No new kernel needed for all-reduce (P2P memcpy + add), but verify the add runs on the right device's stream

items.current: No tool reports whether these two 5060 Ti's can actually talk peer-to-peer, at what bandwidth, or with what topology. P2P between consumer GeForce cards without NVLink is not guaranteed by the driver and depends on the platform (BIOS/PCIe routing).
items.verification: The probe IS the verification: device count/names, cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer both ways, a timed P2P memcpyAsync both ways, and the same copy via pinned host staging, plus nvidia-smi topology
items.notes: PHASE 0 deliverable and the first code of the whole program; run before any tp=2 design is frozen. Its output decides the CHG-0027 fallback path. WP-2 (2026-09-25): CONFIRMED as the Phase-0 deliverable. The P2P availability question itself is answered by the probe output (CHG-0027): P2P copy both ways at 1/16/64 MB, NCCL transport via NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, nvidia-smi topo. The retune it flags is WP-14, against the MEASURED 36 SMs (the plan assumed 48), not part of this item. WP-1 verdict 2026-09-25 (G1): P2P YES both directions but root-complex-routed (PHB, no NVLink); measured D2D 6.5-7.2 GB/s (1/16/64 MB, both directions; run4's 0%-util window: 7.14-7.18) vs pinned-host staging 3.3-3.5 GB/s end-to-end; PCIe link measured Gen3 x8 (max 16x) - P2P is at that degraded link's line rate, not a Gen4 ceiling. The comm layer's actual transport on this box = hand-rolled P2P-mapped (NCCL dead, CHG-0005); staging is the runtime fallback. Raw data + consolidated verdict: dual-gpu/00-p0-probe/ (report.md).

New kv_split_cpu_test: in-regime 15/15.

items.current: Per-sequence GDN recurrent state (fp32 lin_state + bf16 conv state, sized by the value-head layout) is cudaMalloc'd on the single device at open_session; the engine reports alloc_failed for these.
items.verification: Each device holds its v-head slice for every open session; state advances identically on both devices for the same token stream
items.notes: Split axis = value heads (48 -> 24/24 on Qwen3.8-27B), honoring the gdn_qh_block v-head->q-head convention per layer. WP-2 GDN cross-v-head coupling: NO COUPLING. GDN state is block-diagonal per v-head ([hd_k][hd_v] per v-head, transposed [vh][col][row] at rest: qwen36.cu:209/:286/:362/:426; batched_prefill.cu:774-834 pf_gdn_scan state col (vh*HD+j)*HD+m @801, update @823). Conv state is per-CHANNEL, not per v-head (batched_prefill.cu:539/:615/:686: one block per output head, one thread per channel d). q/k are shared read-only across a GQA group (qh = vh % q_heads or vh / (v_heads/q_heads)). Prefill: chunked GDN grids (chunks, v_heads) @prefill_gdn_chunk.cu:101 and (v_heads, HD/JC) @:376/:423-450 - S is per v-head, carry-in only from own slot; call site qwen35_prefill.cpp:2113-2150 (state_at=slot*vh*hd*hd, conv_at=L*(ck-1)*lqkv, carry_in when pos0!=0). Decode: state_off = gdn_state_slot(c,L)*linear_v_heads*hd*hd, qwen35.cpp:2068-2069, launch_qwen36_gdn_ar @2073. => split axis = contiguous v-head range per device (48 -> 24/24 on Qwen3.8-27B); no state exchange between GPUs; per-device snapshots (CHG-0016) hold per-device halves. WP-8 precondition satisfied - slot-level fallback NOT needed. WP-8 (G, 2026-09-27, after ea4bf0f): IMPLEMENTED. GdnStateWindow{v_start,v_count} (0,0 = all heads = tp=1 default, byte-identical) + strict gdn_window_normalize in qwen35.h (degenerate passes through, no warn; invalid/OOB/misaligned clamp to all heads with one printed warning; block mode requires g=v/q to divide both v_start and v_count; cyclic mode admits only a LEADING window, v_count <= q and a multiple of q). open_session now allocates lin_state per device: slots x vloc x HD^2 x 4B; 27B prints 144.0 MiB full (150,994,944 B) -> 72.0 MiB per card at 24/24 (75,497,472 B). CONV state stays FULL per device - DECISION (a): conv rows are the shared q/k/v channels (qkvdim 10,240), not v-head blocks; splitting the 3.75 MiB instead of the 144.0 MiB buys nothing until the forward path is split (Wave-3 H). The per-model full-layout scratch (2 x 48 slots) routes prefill scan / dflash via window<->scratch reinject/extract (one-shot ~2 x 48 x 1.57 MiB D2D on 27B, accepted cost of keeping the commit kernels untouched). Decode single-AR is windowed at the CALL SITE only (state_off = slot x vloc x HD^2 - DENSE per-slot arena; a +v0 x HD^2 term would land in the next slot/OOB, note-2 correction); batched AR kernel takes trailing-default v0/vloc (local state head vh -> global activation head vhg = vh + v0; state-arena indexing stays local). tp=1: (0,0) gives vloc = v, v0 = 0, q-heads full, cols heuristic identical (pure tiling, no numeric change) - every launch arg bit-identical, verified in gdn_split_cpu_test CPU half + 16/16 gate. 27B per-seq GDN state 147.75 MiB (144.0 lin + 3.75 conv); per card at 24/24 = 75.75 MiB (within the spec ~100 MB/card).

items.current: CUDA graphs are captured per session for AR decode (with a per-session parking lot, max 64), plus one prefill graph and one DFlash verify graph, all in the single context. Capture is serialized by the recursive device_mutex against legacy-stream work from other threads (a single-context hazard documented at length in the header).
items.verification: Graphs either captured per device (two graphs per session, launched in lockstep) or one graph with P2P memcpy nodes (requires peer access enabled at capture time -- R5); DSpark stays byte-lossless in either scheme
items.notes: Biggest structural question of the whole program: single-context dual-stream graphs are impossible (a context is one device); the choice between 'two graphs per session, event-synced' and 'P2P nodes in one graph' must be made in P3. The documented legacy-stream capture-poisoning hazard is per-context, so two contexts actually WEAKEN the cross-thread hazard (no implicit cross-context sync) -- restate the invariants either way.

items.current: Two RTX 5060 Ti are consumer cards without NVLink. CUDA peer access between them (cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer) is platform-dependent (BIOS, PCIe topology, driver) and is NOT guaranteed on GeForce pairs; if unavailable, the only path is pinned-host staging (every all-reduce doubles the bytes that cross the PCIe link, at ~25 GB/s effective vs GDDR7 at ~448 GB/s per card).
items.verification: p2p_probe (CHG-0006) output: CanAccessPeer true/false each way + measured P2P vs staged bandwidth + nvidia-smi topo. The final plan MUST handle the fallback: all-reduce over staged buffers with the same API, and a startup check that rejects tp=2 with a clear error when even staging is unavailable
items.notes: TOP RISK of the whole program (R1). Resolve in Phase 0, before layout work starts. WP-2: CONFIRMED as top risk (R1). Resolved by the P0 probe (dual-gpu/00-p0-probe/): P2P copy both ways at 1/16/64 MB (6.5-7.2 GB/s, PHB root-complex-routed, PCIe Gen3 x8 link), NCCL transport recorded (dead - see CHG-0005), per-card memory budget. Staged fallbacks decided in advance: (1) P2P unavailable -> host-staging copy path (existing staging pattern); (2) NCCL unavailable -> hand-rolled all-reduce behind the same gpu_link.h header (WP-3); (3) even staging unavailable -> startup rejection with a clear error. The probe output selects the path; no design work starts before it. WP-1 verdict 2026-09-25 (R1/R7) - RESOLVED, downgraded to a perf fact: P2P IS available both ways (G1), so the TP fast path is P2P-mapped at the MEASURED 6.5-7.2 GB/s - not a datasheet number, because the topology is PHB (root-complex-routed, no NVLink) and the link is measured PCIe Gen3, currently x8 (max 16x; ~7.9 GB/s raw line rate). Pinned-host staging = 3.3-3.5 GB/s end-to-end (2 serial legs). All-reduce cost per layer is therefore bounded by that link; the two-graphs/event-pairing design (WP-11) is unaffected (ordering, not bandwidth). Staged fallbacks: (1) P2P refused at runtime -> pinned staging; (2) NCCL dead on this pair (R8, CHG-0005) -> hand-rolled, which is the path actually taken; (3) startup rejection if neither works. Consolidated verdict: 00-p0-probe/report.md.
